## Code Review

This pull request updates the project's dependencies and tooling, migrating from npm to pnpm, upgrading Next.js to v16, React to v19, Tailwind CSS to v4, and Biome to v2.5.2. It also refactors the service worker's stale-while-revalidate caching strategy to utilize `event.waitUntil` to prevent premature termination, addresses a potential memory leak in `TemporalVoter` by evicting unconfirmed brands, and guards the OCR client's error handler against redundant calls when disposed. There are no review comments to evaluate, so no feedback is provided on them.

> For more details on the timeline and next steps, please review the [Help Documentation](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/deprecations/consumer-code-review).

Prompt for AI agents (unresolved issues) ```text Check if these issues are valid — if so, understand the root cause of each and fix them. If appropriate, use sub-agents to investigate and fix each issue separately. P3: Next.js automatically overwrites the `jsx` compiler option to `"preserve"` on every dev server start — it implements its own optimized JSX transform. Setting `"jsx": "react-jsx"` here will be silently reverted the next time anyone runs `next dev`, which can confuse contributors who see their change undone. Recommend keeping `"jsx": "preserve"` as Next.js expects, and using a separate tsconfig (e.g., `tsconfig.jest.json`) for tools that need the automatic JSX transform. P2: Dark mode based on system preference has stopped working. The old `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` query automatically applied dark theme variables when the user's OS was in dark mode. The migration replaced this with a class-based `@custom-variant dark` / `.dark` pattern, but no code applies the `.dark` class to `` — no theme provider, no script, no toggle. Users who previously saw a dark UI will now always see the light theme. If dark mode is intentional, either restore the `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block or integrate a theme mechanism (e.g., next-themes) that manages the `.dark` class. If the app is meant to be light-only, remove the orphaned `.dark` block to avoid confusion. P2: The `darkMode: "class"` setting in `tailwind.config.ts` is a Tailwind v3 configuration option that Tailwind v4 does not recognize or apply. The `globals.css` already correctly configures class-based dark mode via `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *))`. This line is dead configuration — it has no effect and could mislead someone debugging dark mode behavior. Recommend removing this line, and ensuring the entire `tailwind.config.ts` is either linked via `@config` in `globals.css` (if you need backward-compat theme values from it) or cleaned up and removed in favor of the v4 CSS-native configuration. ```
